is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae (s.l.), specifically identifying An. gambiae (s.s.) and An. coluzzii (page 1, 8).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) (page 4, 5, 8, 9).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 2 and 3 provide genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) and allele frequencies for L1014F kdr and ace-1 G119S for both species across study sites (page 9).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from five field sites in Bouaké, Côte d’Ivoire (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field collection and laboratory analysis (page 1, 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is provided for five specific sites: Allokokro, Petessou, Dar Es Salam, Kennedy, and N’gattakro (page 2, 5).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new collection of mosquitoes in 2014 for the purpose of this specific research.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and bioassay data are provided in the main text tables (Table 1, 2, 3).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae (s.l.) from five sites in Bouaké, Côte d’Ivoire, in 2014. It combined WHO bioassays with molecular genotyping for L1014F kdr and ace-1 G119S mutations, and biochemical assays for metabolic resistance. High resistance to pyrethroids, organochlorines, and carbamates was observed, with metabolic mechanisms and target-site mutations identified as contributing factors.
